scope_note: All sources are primary studies. Search-index excerpts retain stored_search_excerpt even when the index includes body paragraphs. Opened PubMed author abstracts use publisher_abstract. No external LLM calls.

evidence.evidence: EF-G is essential for enforcing coupled movement of the tRNAs and their mRNA codons
evidence.limits: Primary 3.2-A structure without EF-G/GTP shows spontaneous chimeric-state motion and disrupted codon pairing. Do not claim GTP is the sole source of every mechanical displacement.

evidence.evidence: predominant number of U insertions was determined by the number of guiding nucleotides
evidence.limits: Primary cell-free editing and gRNA/UTP/ATP perturbations support cleavage-ligation with U derived from UTP; insertion card does not assert that this paper directly captured every editosome enzyme.

evidence.evidence: Lys72 as the predominant Schiff base nucleophile in the dRP lyase beta-elimination catalytic reaction
evidence.limits: Opened abstract paragraphs. K72A loses over 90% lyase activity without loss of DNA binding; covalent imino mechanism inferred from directed mutants. Preincised abasic substrate, not universal oxidized-sugar repair.

evidence.evidence: His432Arg forms an observable and unique Tdp1-DNA adduct during catalysis
evidence.limits: Opened Abstract and Introduction, especially catalytic Fig.1 discussion. Crystallographic free phosphohistidine is not itself a trapped DNA intermediate; biochemical mutant data support DNA covalent intermediate. Product 3-prime phosphate can need further processing.

evidence.evidence: Two open monomers interact by "domain swapping" to form a compact, globular dimeric DT structure
evidence.limits: Opened primary crystallographic abstract. Card is structural assembly only, without infection, toxin production, engineering, or potency claims. No assertion that domain exchange always propagates as a prion.

evidence.evidence: first from a phosphoserine residue of the protein to the substrate
evidence.limits: Primary structure, biochemical activity and Fig.1 mechanism. Paper explicitly says only dephosphoserine was observed in these crystals; full bisphosphate cycle is mechanistic context supported by earlier kinetics, not directly filmed here. G16P reorientation need not preserve identity of original phosphate atom.

evidence.evidence: a sulfur atom that is still part of the cluster becomes covalently attached to C6
evidence.limits: Primary resting and first-sulfur-inserted intermediate structures show lost auxiliary Fe and substrate-cluster covalent linkage. Does not generalize cluster destruction to every radical-SAM sulfur enzyme or claim in vivo cluster repair route settled.

evidence.evidence: U3S catalyzed cyclization occurs with inversion of the fourth pyrrole ring
evidence.limits: Primary product structure and competitive spirolactam enantiomer experiments support proposed spiro path. No direct spiro-intermediate trapping; conditions explicitly retain model status.

evidence.evidence: trapped hydroperoxy-heme state relaxes to other such states
evidence.limits: Primary cryoreduction, EPR and kinetic comparison. Hydroperoxy decay accompanies meso-hydroxyheme product; ring-opening sequence is stated mechanistic context. Direct PMC open returned CAPTCHA, so not labeled full-text retrieval.

evidence.evidence: key substrate-alkylperoxo-Fe2+ intermediate
evidence.limits: Primary slow-substrate 4-nitrocatechol crystal with three states in separate subunits. Alkylperoxo state directly trapped; precise later Criegee rearrangement sequence remains mechanistic interpretation. Same net oxygen insertion alone would not distinguish from Baeyer-Villiger; adjacent metal-bound substrate/O2 redox coupling does.

evidence.evidence: net result of the process is the conversion of the isomerized peptide to the normal peptide
evidence.limits: Primary model-peptide experiment: normal linkage plus isoAsp after each hydrolysis; methylation repeats selectively. Racemization limits yield; do not claim complete restoration of all native proteins.

evidence.evidence: cleaves a specified distance from the helical end
evidence.limits: Primary intact Dicer crystal shows 65-A PAZ-to-RNaseIII span consistent with 25-bp substrate. Card abstracts geometric end-distance measurement, not every Dicer producing same RNA length or generic nuclease chemistry.

evidence.evidence: forms a fifth ligand for an iron atom in the FTR [4Fe–4S] centre
evidence.limits: Primary structures of one/two-electron-reduced states and four complexes. Boundary is transient fifth sulfur ligation that couples sequential single-electron supply to disulfide chemistry, not substrate-specific thiol exchange alone.

evidence.evidence: repaired spontaneously by guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-tubulin incorporation
evidence.limits: Primary single-molecule TIRF and EM show lattice nanodamage/exchange and increased rescue. No guarantee of net polymer increase without soluble tubulin; boundary is body-lattice renewal, not ordinary end growth or motor-driven proteolysis.

evidence.evidence: concomitant hydride transfer to the Mo=S of the molybdenum center
evidence.limits: Primary functional enzyme-lumazine turnover structure and nonfunctional desulfo-xanthine complex. Hydride/oxygen route supported by contextual rapid kinetics and reduced product Mo-OR adduct; exact timing not universally proven by static coordinates.

evidence.evidence: Photoreception reversibly disrupts salt bridges, triggering dimer dissociation
evidence.limits: Two primary structure/mutagenesis studies support intrinsic tryptophan absorption and salt-bridge destabilization. Do not assert one exact radical pair or proton-transfer sequence; later mechanistic models differ.

evidence.evidence: gp18 subunits slide over each other with no apparent change in their structure
evidence.limits: Primary partial subunit crystal fitted to extended/contracted cryo-EM plus energy discussion. Do not claim tube necessarily crosses both membranes; later cryo-ET shows periplasm entry and separate inner-membrane remodeling. The generic metastable transition overlaps bistability, but explicit lattice-contact reorganization and axial tube stroke are retained for root boundary review.

evidence.evidence: trap the alpha-aminoacrylate reaction intermediate and determine its structure by cryocrystallography
evidence.limits: Primary aminoacrylate crystal and earlier OASS structure with half-reaction mechanism. Quinonoid intermediates are not claimed directly observed universally. All analogous beta-substitution substrates remain one card.

evidence.evidence: pyruvyl C(3) adds to the same face of the phosphorus from which the C(2)O departs
evidence.limits: Primary substrate-analogue structure and mutants oppose phosphoenzyme double displacement; subsequent QM/MM proposes dissociative metaphosphate transition state. Avoid calling free metaphosphate an experimentally trapped stable intermediate.

evidence.evidence: hydrolytic release of formate from GTP followed by cyclization to dihydroneopterin triphosphate
evidence.limits: Primary substrate complexes and zinc-site variants plus later independent family active-site study. Later mutants distinguish early hydrolysis from Amadori/ring-closure function. Avoid obsolete 1995 cystine mechanism: essential zinc was discovered subsequently.

rejected_or_held.reason: Excellent primary ternary-complex/kinetic evidence, but zip-in/zip-out beta-strand displacement may repeat toehold branch migration with a changed polymer; withheld rather than inflate count.
Metal-stabilized carbanion path is explicit, but currently too close to existing alcohol-dehydration-to-alkene plus Lewis-acid catalysis for confident additional counting.
Mechanistic evidence would improve existing biological-nitrogen-fixation; separate card would subdivide same specific enzyme process.
Organocobalt nucleophilic versus electron-transfer path remains contested across retrieved primary calculations; avoid selecting one as settled mechanism.
Hydroxylation followed by spontaneous formaldehyde release may be substrate/damage-repair application of existing oxidative oxygen insertion, so no new card yet.

Strong primary resolved intermediates support stepwise hydride transfer; held for separate comparison against photocatalysis and proton-coupled electron-transfer cards, rather than automatic inclusion.
